security_frame.attacker: Any observer of the sha512_masked_core digest port able to sample it while digest_valid is low. In the integrated design that is the surrounding sha512 control logic and, through it, software reading the digest registers before the operation retires.
security_frame.precondition: A released reset and an in-flight hash operation. The exposure window is every cycle between init_cmd and the assertion of digest_valid.
security_frame.input: One padded message block and an init_cmd pulse. No unusual configuration is needed; the exposure is on the ordinary path.
security_frame.protected_asset: The intermediate compression state of a masked SHA-512 engine. Masking exists so that the working registers are never observable in unmasked form; recombining the two shares defeats the countermeasure the module is named for.
security_frame.security_property: During cycles when no result is valid, the digest port must not carry a value derived from the live compression state. It should carry a constant, or the retained final digest, and nothing that varies with the round or the message.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/sha512_masked/rtl/sha512_masked_core.sv drives the digest port from a two-way select on digest_valid_reg. The valid arm returns the eight H hash registers. The invalid arm returns the bitwise xor of the masked shares and the random shares of the eight working registers a through h, which reconstructs their unmasked values. The select carries no debug, lifecycle or zeroize qualifier, so the exposure is unconditional.

security_feature_bypassed: The masking countermeasure of the SHA-512 masked core. The unmasked working state is reconstructed and driven off the module on every invalid cycle.
proof_goal: Establish on one unmodified core that the digest port carries live, message-dependent compression state during invalid cycles, and that this is distinguishable from both the published initial hash value and any constant placeholder.
proof_style: Directed port-driven simulation of one real DUT with per-cycle sampling of the digest port, a scripted structural audit, and a negative control that neutralises the invalid-cycle arm and requires both to stop reporting.
invariant: A masked engine must not recombine its shares onto an output port.
minimum_attack_sequence: Start a hash operation by pulsing init_cmd with a message block loaded.
Sample the digest port repeatedly while digest_valid is still low.
Each sample is the unmasked value of the eight working registers at that compression round, so the sequence of samples is a trace of the engine's internal state.
controls: The engine reaches a valid digest, so the DUT is functional rather than stuck.
The final digest matches the published SHA-512 value for the empty string, so the engine computes correctly and the exposure is not an artefact of a broken core.
At least eight invalid-cycle samples are captured, so the trace is long enough to reason about.
A second message block also completes and produces a different final digest, establishing that the two configurations really differ.
The final digest still matches the published test vector after the full sampling sweep, so sampling did not perturb the operation.
witness_construction_note: The sampling point is the substance of this case. For the first cycles after init_cmd the working registers still hold the SHA-512 initial hash value, so a witness that captures the first non-zero sample and stops records a published constant and demonstrates no exposure at all. This testbench therefore samples every invalid cycle and keeps the whole trace, then makes three separable statements: samples exist that are neither the initial hash value nor a constant, the value advances from one round to the next, and the trace diverges when the same rounds are reached with a different message block. The third is what rules out the reading that the port merely carries a fixed internal sequence. A bound check records that the initial-hash phase does exist in the trace, so the presence of that phase is documented rather than hidden.
expected_evidence: The digest select's invalid arm reads both the masked and the random shares of the eight working registers and combines them with xor.
The select carries no debug, lifecycle or zeroize qualifier.
Per-cycle sampling yields samples that are neither the initial hash value nor zero.
The sampled value changes across compression rounds.
The sampled trace differs between two different message blocks at the same positions.
The initial-hash phase is present in the trace and is recorded as a bound.
The final digest matches the published test vector for the empty string.
With the invalid arm neutralised, the audit fails on the unmasking gates and all three witness statements stop holding, while the engine still produces the correct digest.
success_criteria: All structural gates pass on the unmodified checkout.
The witness simulation reports exactly three witness statements and prints PROOF_RESULT: PASS.
The negative control makes all three witness statements stop holding and flips the unmasking gates.
The negative control leaves the published test vector control passing, proving the remediation is targeted rather than a break of the hash.
non_findings: No claim that the final digest is wrong. It matches the published value for the empty string.
No claim about a specific software register path in the sha512 wrapper. This case drives the core over its module ports.
No claim of a full key or message recovery. What is demonstrated is that live compression state is observable, not a completed attack.
No claim that the masking scheme is weak in its own right. The finding is that its shares are recombined onto an output port.
